text:
Jackson Blake has become a lot more than a fourth-round find. The Hurricanes winger has 22 points in 23 games at 17:50 a night, and he's on the ice for 83% of Carolina's power-play chances after 40% last season. CBS Sports logged an "Eleven-game, 13-point scoring streak" earlier this month, and Heavy.com called it an "Unforgettable Run."

At five on five, Carolina owns 68% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice. Evolving-Hockey's adjusted measures backed that last season, with his play-driving impact in the 93rd percentile, though they also note he plays beside strong teammates.

Our numbers flag luck pulling both ways. His own finishing is low, 6 goals on 9.3 expected, while his teammates have scored 5.3 more goals than expected with him out there, which pads the assists. Both kinds of luck tend to even out, so the mix could shift toward goals even if the total cools. His ice time has dipped about a minute over the last ten games, and his linemates were shuffling again in his latest game.
